skill.name: binary-re-triage
skill.description: Guide first-pass triage of unknown binaries with file, rabin2, readelf, jq, and import or string inspection.
skill.summary: Fast binary triage workflow for identifying architecture, ABI, dependencies, strings, imports, and next analysis steps.
skill.author: 2389-research

security_audit.summary: The Ruby backtick alerts are mostly Markdown false positives, but several examples direct agents to run local binary-analysis tools. The skill is useful for reverse engineering, yet it should add sandbox and privacy guidance before broad publication.

remediation.issue: External parsers run against unknown binaries without safety requirements.
remediation.suggestion: Tell users to work on read-only copies inside a sandbox or container, and require confirmation before running file, rabin2, or readelf.

remediation.issue: Journaling may preserve sensitive extracted strings and artifact metadata.
remediation.suggestion: Add guidance to redact secrets, customer identifiers, internal paths, and proprietary URLs before saving notes to memory.

remediation.issue: Example commands use a generic binary path without validation steps.
remediation.suggestion: Add a preflight checklist for trusted working directories, immutable input copies, hash capture, and no execution of the target binary.

semantic_findings.title: Untrusted Binary Parsing Without Safety Guidance
semantic_findings.description: The skill is for first contact with unknown binaries and directs local parsing with tools such as rabin2 and readelf. It does not require sandboxing, read-only copies, or user confirmation before parsing attacker-controlled files.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The skill explicitly targets unknown binaries and provides commands that parse them locally. The missing safety guidance is clear, though the commands do not execute the target binary.

semantic_findings.title: Persistent Journal May Capture Sensitive Artifact Data
semantic_findings.description: The skill asks the agent to record findings for episodic memory, including filenames, hashes, library names, strings of interest, and paths. These values may reveal proprietary firmware details or secrets extracted from a binary.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The journaling instruction and sample fields are explicit. The impact depends on the host memory policy, so confidence is high for exposure potential but moderate for exploitability.

content.value_statement: Unknown executables and firmware blobs need quick facts before deeper reverse engineering. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through fast metadata, ABI, dependency, string, and import checks.
actual_capabilities: Identifies architecture, bit width, endianness, operating system, and stripped status.
Maps ELF interpreter paths to likely libc and ABI details.
Extracts dependencies, entry points, exports, imports, and notable strings with rabin2 workflows.
Groups imports into likely capabilities such as networking, file I/O, crypto, and threading.
Produces structured triage notes with facts, hypotheses, open questions, and next analysis steps.
limitations: Requires local tools such as file, rabin2, readelf, jq, and grep.
Does not decompile functions or explain full program behavior.
Does not execute binaries or observe runtime behavior.
Can expose sensitive strings unless users redact triage notes.

use_cases.title: Classify Firmware Utilities
use_cases.description: Identify architecture, libc, dependencies, and likely capabilities before selecting a reverse engineering toolchain.

use_cases.title: Prepare Malware Intake Notes
use_cases.description: Collect safe first-pass facts, suspicious strings, imports, and hypotheses without running the sample.

use_cases.title: Plan Portability Work
use_cases.description: Check ABI, dynamic linker, library dependencies, and static linking status before rebuilding or emulating a binary.

prompt_templates.title: Identify This Binary
prompt_templates.prompt: Triage this binary at ./sample. Report file type, architecture, bit width, endianness, link type, and interpreter path.

prompt_templates.title: Map ABI And Libraries
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze ./firmware-daemon for ABI, libc, float ABI, imported libraries, and likely runtime environment. Do not execute the binary.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize Capabilities
prompt_templates.prompt: Use imports, dependencies, and strings to infer likely capabilities in ./agent. Separate facts from hypotheses and cite evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Reverse Engineering Handoff
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a triage handoff for ./target with facts, risks, open questions, sysroot needs, and the best next analysis phase.

output_examples.input: Triage an ARM firmware daemon before deeper analysis.
output: Reports ARM 32-bit little-endian ELF metadata and the detected musl interpreter.
Lists linked network and TLS libraries with supporting import evidence.
Recommends static analysis next because the binary is stripped and not yet safe to run.

output_examples.input: Assess a shared library from an embedded device image.
output: Summarizes exported symbols, imported libraries, and likely file or network capabilities.
Flags missing ABI details that require a matching sysroot.
Separates confirmed facts from hypotheses for later validation.

output_examples.input: Prepare notes for a suspicious executable without executing it.
output: Captures hash, size, architecture, string counts, and notable indicators.
Groups imports into capability categories for analyst review.
Adds redaction reminders before storing sensitive strings in notes.

best_practices: Run triage tools on read-only copies inside an isolated workspace.
Record command outputs as evidence, then separate facts from hypotheses.
Redact secrets, customer identifiers, and proprietary paths before saving notes.
anti_patterns: Do not execute the target binary during triage.
Do not treat one string or import as proof of behavior.
Do not save extracted credentials or private URLs into shared memory.

faq.question: Does this skill execute binaries?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on metadata, imports, dependencies, and strings. Users should avoid running the target during triage.

faq.question: Which tools does it expect?
faq.answer: It expects common local tools such as file, rabin2, readelf, jq, and grep.

faq.question: Can it analyze non-ELF files?
faq.answer: It is strongest for ELF and firmware artifacts. Other formats may need different tools or follow-up analysis.

faq.question: Is this enough for a full reverse engineering report?
faq.answer: No. It produces first-pass facts and hypotheses before static or dynamic analysis.

faq.question: How should sensitive strings be handled?
faq.answer: Review and redact secrets, internal URLs, customer data, and private paths before saving or sharing results.

faq.question: Can Claude Code or Codex use it safely?
faq.answer: Yes, when users confirm commands and run tools in an isolated workspace with untrusted binaries kept read-only.
